display.title: Episode 316: Little Avraham (Zayin Adar and Parshas Zachor)
display.summary_short: Before Zayin Adar, Uncle Yossi teaches why a birthday is a special day, tells how three-year-old Avraham searched for and found Hashem, and urges everyone to hear Parshas Zachor.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the week of Zayin Adar 5748, the yahrzeit and birthday of Moshe Rabbeinu. Uncle Yossi explains that Haman chose Adar thinking it was only a sad month, not knowing it was also Moshe Rabbeinu's birthday. A birthday is a joyful day in Heaven and on earth, when a neshamah comes down to learn Torah and do mitzvos; it is a day when one's mazal is strong, a day for teshuvah and good resolutions. Children should know their Hebrew birthday, and newborns can be enrolled in Tzivos Hashem. After the Hakochainik march, two sisters from Beis Rivkah recite the Shema. The story: little Avraham, three years old, walks by the sea and wonders who made the world. He thinks of the sun, the moon and the stars, but each one sets, until he understands that the Creator is One, unseen and everywhere, and sets out to tell the world. Uncle Yossi then reminds everyone to hear Parshas Zachor in shul this Shabbos, and gives Shabbos candle time.
display.lesson: Your Hebrew birthday is a special day to grow and make good resolutions; like Avraham, search until you recognize the One Creator.

date.note: Consistent with the audio: 'this coming Thursday is Zayin Adar'; Parshas Zachor this Shabbos; candles Friday, February 26.

sources_cited.note: Cited as 'our Chachamim': Haman rejoiced that Adar was the month of Moshe's passing, not knowing it was also his birthday.
Cited as 'our Chachamim': a person's mazal is strong on his birthday.
